payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: In the edited image, is a mug visibly positioned to the right of the headphones?
node.criteria: Inspect the edited image and compare the visible mug or mugs with the headphones. Pass only if a mug is clearly positioned to the right of the headphones. Fail if the image reliably shows no mug to their right. Use unknown if the objects or their relative positions cannot be determined reliably. This checks only the final spatial relation for a mug in the edited image; it does not establish that the source mug itself was moved.
node.binding: Edited image only: the visible mug or mugs and the headphones; assess their left-to-right positions.

node_traces.evidence: In the edited image, a visible mug is on the right side of the headphones, with the mug clearly farther right in the image.

response.content: {"text":"The current binding and criterion test only whether any mug is right of the headphones, so the trace passes on the rightmost mug even though the edited image also shows a mug left of the headphones and a blurred blue remnant where the original mug was. That establishes some progress, not complete fulfillment; the aggregate/reference mismatch likely reflects that this single binary check cannot distinguish partial from complete. For typed structural edits, preserve the final-image spatial check but make its scope and output semantics explicit: assess all visible mugs and their positions, and distinguish a clearly supported partial result from complete fulfillment only when the node has evidence relevant to the requested move (including source-to-edited comparison). Do not infer that the rightmost mug is the moved source mug from the edited image alone. Keep uncertainty for ambiguous object identity or position; the trace is valid, queried, and has no dependency or transport failure, so this is a criterion/coverage limitation rather than a visual-evidence or execution failure."}
